title: Advanced Bongcloud: The Outside Passed Pawn
summary: Black can let the white king collect a pawn while advancing a different pawn toward promotion.

nodes.question: Can White catch the b-pawn by capturing c6?
nodes.explanation: Black has a winning five-piece ending. Kc3 supports the b-pawn from in front, while the white king is too far away to stop its advance after collecting c6.

branches.title: Independent continuation: collect a pawn, lose the race
commentary: Begin with White Ke6 and Black Kb4/a6/b5/c6. Black moves next. The larger earlier pawn ending remains outside this exact proof.
Kc3 is visible in the next source state. Black brings the king near the promotion route; b2 is already within its protection.
Kd6 approaches c6. This is a legal representative White reply, also seen in the next native diagram; later move order is supplied independently.
b4 begins the passed-pawn advance. White can take c6, but capturing one pawn does not stop a different pawn.
Kxc6 removes c6. The exact four-piece ending still favors Black; a6 and b4 remain real threats on the board.
b3 advances toward b2 and b1. White’s king on c6 cannot return quickly enough to the promotion route.
Kc5 heads back toward the pawn. This independently supplied move does not change the exact winning result for Black.
b2 puts the pawn one step from promotion. Kc3 protects it, and the white king cannot capture it. The saved tablebase confirms a Black win; no unobserved game moves are claimed.

branches.title: Independent reply: the king walks away
commentary: Test another legal White king reply to the source Kc3. This is an independent comparison, not source narration.
Kc3 gives the black king access to the pawn’s path and leaves the b-pawn free to run.
Kf6 moves farther from the b-file. White still has no pawn of its own to create a counter-race.
b4 preserves the exact Black win. White’s king is farther away than in the c6-capture line, so Black can advance without first collecting any other material.

exercises.answer: The c6 pawn is not the pawn that must promote. Black advances the distant b-pawn while White spends king moves collecting c6.
